summary.text: Adrian William King is an independent candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. He says he turns around struggling organisations for a living, has lived locally for 15 years and became an Australian citizen in 2016. He ran in the 2024 council elections, a race his website places in Port Phillip's Port Melbourne ward while the ABC names Melbourne City Council.

previous_candidacies.note: His website says he ran in the Port Melbourne ward; the ABC says Melbourne City Council. No source gives his label or the result.

priorities.text: Rebuilding Victoria Police and bringing back local high-street policing to cut drug-related crime
Cutting 20,000 public service jobs to return $1,000 a year to each working Victorian
A royal commission into Victoria Police command, the judiciary and IBAC
Restoring Albert Park Reserve and limiting the Grand Prix's impact to four months a year
Secure housing for people with chronic mental illness

sources.title: Albert Park: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Adrian King, Independent Candidate

summary.text: Andrew Cook is the Liberal candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. The party describes him as a married father and a businessman of over five decades' experience, and says his family has long ties to the area. Neither the party nor the ABC gives further detail of his career.

priorities.text: Reducing crime, including the party's pledge of 3,000 more police and tougher bail laws
Growing the economy and easing cost-of-living pressure

sources.title: Albert Park: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andrew Cook, Liberal for Albert Park, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Colleen Bolger is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a lawyer acting for people with asbestos-related and other work-caused diseases, a union delegate, and has campaigned against the mandatory detention of refugees for over 20 years. She has stood for the party several times, most recently in the Warrandyte by-election of 2023.

priorities.text: Pay rises that keep up with inflation
A big public housing building program and caps on rents
Taxing corporate profits to pay for public services
Taking on big business to act on climate change
Opposing racism and the scapegoating of migrants

summary.text: Georgie Dragwidge is an independent candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. For about 15 years she has run two businesses at the South Melbourne Market, and she is a single mother whose parents migrated from Greece. She also stood as an independent in Albert Park in 2022, taking close to 6 per cent of the primary vote.

occupation.text: Small business owner, South Melbourne Market

priorities.text: Safety at home and on the streets through planned, funded police, justice and welfare services
A bigger say for small business in policy
Integrity in politics, with properly funded anti-corruption bodies
Consulting the electorate on major votes in Parliament
Climate action and protecting Albert Park Reserve, local parks and beaches

summary.text: Nina Taylor is the Labor member for Albert Park in the Legislative Assembly, first elected to that seat in 2022. From 2018 to 2022 she sat in the Legislative Council for Southern Metropolitan Region, where she was Government Whip. She has been Cabinet Secretary since August 2026 and is recontesting Albert Park in 2026.

occupation.text: Union organiser (Community and Public Sector Union); earlier a school teacher

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Training and Skills
Government Whip in the Legislative Council

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia doesn't say what label she stood under at this council election; the code is her party membership.

priorities.text: Clean and affordable energy
Better transport choices across several modes
Safe, climate-ready housing for everyone
Fair access to education and training pathways

summary.text: Sonya Semmens is the Greens candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. Raised in Dandenong, she has spent most of her working life in the not-for-profit sector, in Australian charities and overseas aid agencies, and has also been an educator and run a small business. She stood for the Greens in the federal seats of Higgins in 2022 and Macnamara in 2025.

priorities.text: ensure no one experiences homelessness in a country as wealthy as Australia
Better security for renters facing insecure housing
Fairness, so that everyone gets a go

summary.text: Tam Lindrum is One Nation's candidate for Albert Park at the 2026 Victorian election. A registered nurse who has also worked in pharmaceutical sales management and marketing, she is the founder of the Women's Billiards and Snooker Network. She is related to the billiards champion Walter Lindrum, though the ABC calls her his daughter while Wikipedia's article on him calls her his great-niece and god-daughter.
summary.note: The ABC calls her Walter Lindrum's daughter; Wikipedia's article on him calls her his great-niece and god-daughter.
